topStories.headline: The Mess Hall Opens at Presidio Tunnel Tops, Completing the Park's Vision
topStories.dek: The long-awaited food hall debuted August 15 inside a restored 1898 building, bringing three restaurants, a cocktail bar, a café, and a specialty market to the Presidio.
topStories.body:
Four years after Presidio Tunnel Tops opened to the public, its final piece fell into place on August 15 when The Mess Hall at the Presidio swung open its doors at 201 Halleck Street. The 6,200-square-foot indoor-outdoor space occupies a historic building that once served as an animal feed store, butcher shop, and mailroom during the Presidio's military era — and the restoration preserved original wood throughout, with design details drawn from the 1930s and 1940s.

The food hall is led by restaurateur Nate Leonard, entrepreneur Rob Gaon, and James Beard Award–winning chef Peter Serpico, who developed the culinary concepts. Three fast-casual restaurant concepts anchor the hall: Boda (Korean and Asian-inspired dishes), Dayboat Seafood (raw oysters, shrimp cocktail, crudo, and build-your-own handrolls), and Breadwinner (sandwiches, burgers, and salads). A daytime café features pastries from Breadbelly — ranked seventh in the SF Chronicle's 2026 Top 100 — and coffee from Wrecking Ball Coffee Roasters, opening daily at 7 a.m.

As of this week, Breadwinner, the bar, café, and market are fully operational; Boda and Dayboat Seafood are expected to begin full service shortly, according to 7x7's August 20 report. The hall boasts wraparound views of San Francisco Bay, the Palace of Fine Arts, and Alcatraz. Leonard has described his goal as being part of residents' and visitors' daily routines at the Tunnel Tops park, which draws millions of visitors each year.

The Mess Hall marks the latest in a series of culinary additions to the Presidio, joining Dalida, Il Parco, and the recently opened Maria Isabel. A Fieldwork Brewing Company taproom is also expected to open nearby in the coming months.

topStories.headline: Richmond District Named San Francisco's Most Desirable Neighborhood in Chronicle Reader Poll
topStories.dek: A San Francisco Chronicle poll published August 6 found that Richmond District residents beat out sunnier neighborhoods to earn the top spot for where Chronicle readers most want to live.
topStories.body:
The Richmond District — famously foggy, famously walkable — has been crowned the neighborhood San Francisco Chronicle readers most want to call home, according to a reader poll published on August 6. Nineteen of 130 respondents chose the Richmond District, outpacing 29 other neighborhoods in the informal survey. The runners-up included Bernal Heights (13 votes), North Beach (10), and a three-way tie among Glen Park, the Sunset, and Noe Valley.

Chronicle culture critic Peter Hartlaub noted the result caught editors off guard: sunnier, warmer neighborhoods were expected to dominate. Instead, readers praised the Richmond for its movie theaters, great parks in every direction, relatively affordable homes (by San Francisco standards), and a food scene that has gained significant momentum in 2026 with major openings on Clement Street.

The result reflects a broader trend of renewed interest in the neighborhood's western corridors. The Inner Richmond, long called the city's 'New Chinatown' for its dense concentration of Chinese restaurants and markets, has attracted high-profile restaurant openings this year, including Rose Pizzeria at 1 Clement Street and a buzz around the Clement Street Farmers Market as a Sunday morning destination.

topStories.headline: Cottage Bakery Cuprum Rises from Inner Richmond Home Kitchen
topStories.dek: Valeriya Romashchenko's home-based Cuprum Bakery, launched in 2024, is gaining a growing following in the Richmond District for its science-driven sourdough and baked goods.
topStories.body:
Walk up to the right address in the Inner Richmond and you may find fresh sourdough stacked on a rack on a front stoop — that's Cuprum Bakery, the cottage operation run by Valeriya Romashchenko out of her home kitchen. The Richmond Review profiled Romashchenko in its August 15 edition, chronicling how a bioengineering graduate of Moscow State University and the San Francisco Baking Institute turned pandemic-era flexibility into a growing small business.

Romashchenko, who moved to San Francisco in 2016, first started baking at age 12 in Russia and says her scientific background is central to her process: she approaches each batch the way a lab researcher would, tracking starter behavior across seasons and adjusting variables systematically. The bakery's name — Cuprum — comes from the Latin word for copper, her favorite element on the periodic table.

Cuprum operates as a California Cottage Food Operation, with orders placed via Hotplate and pick-up from her home in the Inner Richmond. The bakery's growing profile is part of a broader wave of small food entrepreneurs finding audiences in the Richmond District, where a strong base of food-literate residents has historically supported independent producers.

events.title: EXCLUSION: The Presidio's Role in WWII Japanese American Incarceration
events.location: Presidio Officers' Club, 50 Moraga Avenue, Presidio
events.description: The award-winning free exhibition examines how the Presidio served as the Army's Western Defense Command and its role in the unjust incarceration of 120,000 Japanese Americans during World War II. Open Fridays through Sundays through August 31.

events.title: Fort Point History Talks
events.description: Free 15-minute ranger-led history talks at Fort Point are offered Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays throughout the summer season.

events.title: Presidio Campfire Program
events.description: Free campfire programs hosted by the National Park Service take place Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays at Presidio Tunnel Tops throughout summer.

events.title: Clement Street Farmers Market
events.description: The Inner Richmond's beloved year-round Sunday farmers market runs along three city blocks, featuring local produce, artisan baked goods, flowers, dairy, and specialty foods from Bay Area vendors.

events.title: Presidio Forest Stewards Volunteer Day
events.description: Join the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy to help restore the Presidio forest through hands-on stewardship. No experience required; tools and training provided.

events.title: Presidio Habitat Stewards Volunteer Day
events.description: Volunteer to restore native habitat in the Presidio alongside the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy team, with tasks suited to all skill levels.

events.title: Los Californianos: Anza 250 / America 250 Living History Celebration
events.location: Presidio Officers' Club, 50 Moraga Avenue, Presidio
events.description: A living history program marking the Presidio's 250th anniversary, with a procession, flag ceremonies, historical reenactors in period dress, music by Los Arribeños de San Francisco and the Young American Patriots Fife & Drum Corps, and free guided tours of the Heritage Gallery.

events.title: Presidio Tunnel Tops Stewards Volunteer Day
events.description: Help care for the Tunnel Tops park landscape alongside Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy stewardship staff in this free recurring volunteer session.

moreNews.headline: Rose Pizzeria's Inner Richmond Location Booked Solid Through Summer
moreNews.body: Rose Pizzeria — the Berkeley sensation that the New York Times named one of America's 22 best pizzerias in 2024 — opened its first San Francisco outpost at 1 Clement Street earlier this year, and demand has not let up. Husband-and-wife owners Gerad Gobel and Alexis Rorabaugh transformed the former Village Pizzeria space, restoring original green-and-white checkered floors and outfitting the 44-seat dining room with marble-topped tables. The SF location offers a slightly expanded menu compared to the Berkeley original, including customizable pies and signature options like the She Wolf (burrata, slow-roasted tomato, garlic confit, olives, capers) and the Beach Club (pistachio mortadella, pickled jalapeño, and pineapple). The restaurant is open daily 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. and accepts walk-ins at the counter, bar, and sidewalk tables.

moreNews.headline: Trump's New Presidio Trust Board Settles In as Busy Summer Season Continues
moreNews.body: After President Trump fired all six Biden-appointed members of the Presidio Trust Board of Directors in April, the White House appointed six new members in May. The new board includes philanthropist Lynne Benioff (a former board chair), diplomat and tech entrepreneur Trevor Traina, Stanford educator Laura Arrillaga-Andreessen, xAI general counsel James Burnham, Local Capital Group managing partner John Bickford, and Redpanda CFO Kyle Corcoran. Presidio Trust spokesperson Lisa Petrie said park operations have continued without interruption through the transition, and the new board is being oriented to the park as the Presidio's biggest summer programming season — including the opening of The Mess Hall and the ongoing 250th anniversary commemorations — gets underway.

moreNews.headline: Richmond District Home Prices Post Strongest Year-Over-Year Gains of 2026
moreNews.body: San Francisco single-family home prices posted their strongest year-over-year gain of 2026, surging more than 26%, according to Mosaik Real Estate's August market report. The Richmond District, known for its classic architecture and access to Golden Gate Park and the Presidio, continues to attract buyers drawn to its neighborhood feel and culinary reputation. The trend aligns with the Chronicle reader poll published August 6 that named the Richmond the neighborhood San Francisco readers most want to live in.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: Iconic Inner Richmond Burmese restaurant famous for its tea leaf salad, samosas, and pumpkin pork stew — no reservations, expect a line.

restaurants.name: B Star Bar
restaurants.description: Sister restaurant to Burma Superstar serving Burmese, Thai, Chinese, and California fusion dishes with shorter wait times.

restaurants.name: Wako Japanese Restaurant
restaurants.description: Michelin-starred intimate sushi restaurant led by Chef Tomoyuki Hayashi, offering a highly regarded omakase experience in the heart of the Inner Richmond.

restaurants.name: Chapeau!
restaurants.description: Beloved classic French bistro with consistent prix fixe and à la carte menus, celebrated for hospitality and timeless cuisine since 1996.

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: The Berkeley sensation — named one of America's 22 best pizzerias by the New York Times — opened its first San Francisco location at the corner of Clement and Arguello in 2026.

restaurants.name: Arsicault Bakery
restaurants.description: Widely considered the best croissant in San Francisco, this bakery draws long lines for its caramelized, buttery pastries and kouign amann.

restaurants.name: Breadbelly
restaurants.description: Inner Richmond bakery known for Asian-American pastries including gyeranbbang (Korean cheesy egg cornbread), Malaysian kaya toast, and exceptional croissants.

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: Acclaimed Turkish restaurant on Clement Street offering mezes, kebabs, and a natural wine list favored by local sommeliers.

restaurants.name: Mandalay
restaurants.description: San Francisco's first Burmese restaurant, open since 1984, serving beloved classics including coconut chicken noodle soup and an intensely nutty tea leaf salad.

restaurants.name: Fiorella
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Italian spot on Clement Street with wood-fired pizza, house-made pastas, and a welcoming, convivial atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Dalida
restaurants.description: Upscale Mediterranean restaurant in the Presidio earning critical acclaim for its California-inflected dishes and acclaimed cocktail program.

restaurants.name: Maria Isabel
restaurants.description: New Mexican restaurant from the team behind Dalida, rooted in the coastal flavors of Guerrero and Acapulco, with heirloom corn, California seafood, and a 2026 Michelin Exceptional Cocktails Award.

restaurants.name: The Mess Hall at the Presidio
restaurants.description: The Presidio's new all-day food hall in a restored 1898 building at Tunnel Tops, featuring Breadwinner sandwiches, Dayboat Seafood, Boda Korean cuisine, a cocktail bar, Breadbelly café, and a specialty market.

restaurants.name: Good Luck Dim Sum
restaurants.description: No-frills Inner Richmond dim sum shop beloved for an astounding variety of dumplings at very affordable prices, cash-friendly.

restaurants.name: Pearl 6101
restaurants.description: Warm, consistently praised bistro in the Outer Richmond known for its inviting atmosphere and crowd-pleasing seasonal American dishes.

restaurants.name: Eats
restaurants.description: Cozy brunch café from the owners of Burma Superstar, serving elevated breakfast dishes including eggs benedict, huevos rancheros, and breakfast cocktails.

restaurants.name: Cinderella Russian Bakery & Café
restaurants.description: A Richmond District institution since 1953 serving traditional Russian baked goods, piroshki, blini, and borscht in a warm neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Plough & Stars
restaurants.description: Traditional Irish pub on Clement Street with live folk and trad music most nights, a strong whiskey selection, and a loyal neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: 540 Club
restaurants.description: Casual dive bar and live-music venue on Geary offering an eclectic lineup of local bands and DJs in a no-frills Inner Richmond setting.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: A 22-room Georgian Revival inn inside the Presidio national park, housed in the former Pershing Hall bachelor officers' quarters, with complimentary breakfast and evening wine-and-cheese receptions.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: A boutique hotel set in the 1895–1897 Montgomery Street Barracks on the Presidio's Main Post, steps from Tunnel Tops and with sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: A restored Victorian hotel at the edge of Golden Gate Park, offering an intimate, quiet stay close to the Richmond District and park amenities.

hotels.name: Travelodge by Wyndham Presidio San Francisco
hotels.description: Budget-friendly motel near the Presidio and Lombard Street corridor, convenient for visitors exploring the park and adjacent neighborhoods.

hotels.name: Laurel Inn
hotels.description: Stylish mid-century modern hotel on Presidio Avenue offering spacious rooms, pet-friendly policies, and easy access to both the Presidio and the Richmond District.

shops.name: Green Apple Books & Music
shops.description: A beloved two-story Richmond District bookstore founded in 1967, packed with over 250,000 new, used, and rare titles across eclectic themed rooms — a certified San Francisco Legacy Business.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.description: Hybrid art gallery and retail shop on Clement Street selling limited-edition art books, design objects, prints, clothing, jewelry, and original art from Bay Area and international artists.

shops.name: Healthy Spirits
shops.description: Inner Richmond bottle shop specializing in craft beer, bourbon, hard-to-find spirits, and a curated selection of natural wines.

shops.name: Kamei Restaurant Supply
shops.description: Compact but well-stocked shop carrying Japanese and Asian kitchen supplies, ceramics, teapots, chopsticks, and cooking tools at accessible prices.

shops.name: NOISE
shops.type: Independent record store, gallery, and live music space
shops.description: Family-operated Richmond District shop combining a curated vinyl record store, art gallery, and intimate live music performance space.

shops.name: Aroma Tea Shop
shops.description: Specialty tea shop on Clement Street offering a wide selection of premium Chinese teas, teaware, and knowledgeable staff to guide customers through selections.

shops.name: Public Land
shops.description: Clement Street shop selling plants, home goods, and showcasing works by local Bay Area artists in a welcoming neighborhood space.

shops.name: Toy Boat Dessert Café
shops.type: Vintage toy shop and ice cream café
shops.description: Quirky Inner Richmond institution combining a full retro toy collection with scoops of ice cream, espresso drinks, and a beloved neighborhood vibe since 1981.

shops.name: Richmond Republic Homebrew Supply
shops.description: Outer Richmond shop supplying home brewers and winemakers with ingredients, equipment, and expert advice on craft brewing and fermentation.

shops.name: Daiso Japan
shops.description: Popular Japanese budget retailer offering a vast array of household goods, stationery, kitchen tools, snacks, and beauty products on Clement Street.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: A 40,000-square-foot museum inside a beautifully restored 1897 Presidio barracks, chronicling Walt Disney's life through ten interactive galleries, original artifacts, and over 200 video screens — open Thursday through Monday during summer.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: The Presidio's oldest standing structure, housing free exhibitions including EXCLUSION: The Presidio's Role in WWII Japanese American Incarceration, plus heritage gallery tours and special programs.

artEntertainment.name: Balboa Theater
artEntertainment.description: A cherished two-screen independent cinema in the Outer Richmond, open since 1926, screening first-run and double-feature films, cult classics, and hosting live comedy shows in a classically restored setting.

artEntertainment.name: 4 Star Theater
artEntertainment.description: Beloved independent cinema on Clement Street at 23rd Avenue, known for diverse programming spanning mainstream releases, foreign films, and special screenings.

artEntertainment.name: Park Life Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Contemporary art gallery and design shop
artEntertainment.description: Inner Richmond gallery space within the Park Life shop, curating rotating exhibitions of contemporary art, design objects, and limited-edition prints by Bay Area and international artists.

artEntertainment.name: Plough & Stars (Live Music)
artEntertainment.type: Irish pub and live music venue
artEntertainment.description: Traditional Irish pub hosting live folk, traditional Irish, and acoustic music most nights of the week in an intimate Richmond District setting.

artEntertainment.name: NOISE SF (Live Music & Gallery)
artEntertainment.type: Record store, gallery, and live music space
artEntertainment.description: Family-operated Inner Richmond space hosting intimate live music performances alongside its vinyl record collection and rotating art gallery.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Visitor Center
artEntertainment.type: National park visitor center and exhibition space
artEntertainment.description: The Presidio's main visitor hub offering free interpretive exhibits on the park's history spanning Ohlone, Spanish, Mexican, and American eras, plus ranger programs and trip planning resources.

artEntertainment.name: Fort Point National Historic Site
artEntertainment.description: A massive brick Civil War-era fort beneath the Golden Gate Bridge offering free ranger-led history talks and stunning views of the bay's entrance.
artEntertainment.address: Marine Dr at Long Ave, Presidio

gymsRecreation.name: Live Fit Gym – Inner Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Three-story Inner Richmond gym with modernized cardio and weight equipment, group yoga and HIIT classes, personal training, massage therapy, and chiropractic care.

gymsRecreation.name: Purusha Yoga + Pilates Studio
gymsRecreation.description: Outer Richmond studio with 25 years of experience offering Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, Restorative yoga and Pilates mat classes in a welcoming, community-oriented setting.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot Yoga Plus Seacliff
gymsRecreation.description: Heated yoga studio near Sea Cliff offering a variety of hot yoga classes in a clean studio environment with hardwood floors.

gymsRecreation.name: Koret Health and Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: University of San Francisco's recreation center on the edge of Lone Mountain, offering a pool, gym, courts, and fitness classes to members and the public.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: Historic 18-hole public golf course within the Presidio, operating since 1895, set among Monterey cypress and eucalyptus forests with views of the Golden Gate.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
gymsRecreation.type: Public park and outdoor recreation space
gymsRecreation.description: The 14-acre park atop the Presidio's Doyle Drive tunnel features meadows, trails, a native plant garden, Outpost nature playground, and Golden Gate Bridge views — free and open daily.

gymsRecreation.name: Mountain Lake Park
gymsRecreation.type: Public park with lake and trails
gymsRecreation.description: A serene park at the edge of the Presidio featuring a restored freshwater lake, restored native habitat, playground, and easy access to Presidio trail networks.

gymsRecreation.name: Lands End Trail
gymsRecreation.description: Dramatic coastal trail along the northern edge of the Richmond District offering clifftop views of the Golden Gate, shipwreck ruins at low tide, and access to the Sutro Baths ruins.

gymsRecreation.name: Arise Yoga San Francisco
gymsRecreation.description: Inner Richmond yoga studio offering Vinyasa, Hatha, and restorative classes for all levels in a friendly, community-focused environment.

gymsRecreation.name: Ocean Beach
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's largest beach stretches three miles along the western edge of the Outer Richmond and Sunset, popular for walking, running, surfing, and bonfires at designated fire rings.
gymsRecreation.address: Great Highway at Balboa St, Outer Richmond
